title: JobEnvelope
description: The only thing the RetentionOps control plane may ask a connector to do. The operation set is closed and the payload is declarative: there is no field anywhere in this schema that carries SQL, a script, a command, a file path or a connection string. A control plane that has been compromised can therefore only ask for an operation that already exists, on a target the local safety policy already allows.

protocol_version.description: A connector refuses any version it was not built against. Forward compatibility is obtained by shipping a new connector, never by guessing.

connector_id.description: Refused unless it equals this connector's own enrolled identity, so a job addressed to another connector cannot be replayed here.

plan_digest.description: Binds the job to the exact plan a human approved. Required for every destructive operation.

expires_at.description: A job that arrives late is refused rather than executed late: the database it was planned against has moved on.

nonce.description: Single-use. The connector keeps a durable ledger of seen nonces until expiry, which is what makes a captured DELETE unusable twice.

signature.description: Ed25519 over 'RetentionOps-Job-v1\n' followed by the RFC 8785 canonical form of this document with the signature member removed.

identifier.description: An unquoted lowercase PostgreSQL identifier. Anything outside this pattern is refused before it can reach a query builder; the connector never interpolates a name it has not matched here.

operation.description: Closed set. Adding a member is a protocol version change reviewed as a security change, because every member is a new capability granted to the control plane.

predicate.description: A retention predicate, not an expression language. One column, one comparison, one literal value bound as a query parameter.

value.description: Always an RFC 3339 instant. Bound as a parameter, never rendered into the statement.

condition.description: Closed declarative condition tree. It contains identifiers, operators and bound JSON literals, never an expression or SQL fragment.

limits.description: Ceilings the control plane requests. The local safety policy may only lower them, never raise them.

pause_between_batches_ms.description: Approved delay after a committed batch and its control checkpoint.

drift.description: What the plan measured, and how far reality may have moved since. The connector recounts before deleting and refuses the job if the gap is wider than this.

max_basis_points.description: Hundredths of one percent: 50 means 0.5%. The protocol carries no floating-point number anywhere, because two canonicalizers agreeing on the digest of a float is a far harder guarantee than this feature is worth.

approval.description: Evidence that a human approved this exact plan digest. Its absence is refused locally, so the control plane cannot execute without one even against its own database.
